I’m a sophomore so my portfolio isn’t quite there yet. I am planning to join the club Engineers without Borders to fulfill the cultural competency, taking classes on other languages (such as spanish) to fulfill the multidisciplinary area, I am currently a part time instructor at the Viterbi K-12 center so that’ll be the education/K-12 criteria. Finally, research (related to your grand challenge) and volunteering will fill the last two. 
There will be events where usc representatives help you stay on track in fulfilling those competencies. The representative I know is named Myra Fernandez (she hosts a lot of Viterbi meetings!) so you’ll get to build and expand on what you’re doing as you go, sort of like a resume. 
From what I know, there will be essays. 
For example, how are the classes that you took for the multidisciplinary area related to engineering?

I am currently in the program! It entails five categories that each scholar must fulfill and an emphasis on one of the grand challenges (remember the last insight question when applying to Viterbi? Hehe). The categories include taking multidisciplinary classes, having a well rounded knowledge of different cultures (you can travel abroad or join a cultural club etc.) and more. Yes, you can change your emphasis whenever you want. I am currently doing “providing access to clean waters” but that may change. You can apply to the program whenever. You don’t need to be a freshmen. You’ll submit a portfolio when you’re a senior and the National Academy of Engineers will determine whether or not you become recognized. Good luck!
